hypothesis: Different derived stems require different transformations. The shared-stem paradigm pilot showed nearly perfectly correlated errors, so simply adding its inflectional endings did not help.
task: One root and prefix sequence; two or four separately specified sanadi/tense derivations; same person and number throughout a task; row-keyed Devanagari JSON answers.
grammar: Only previously reviewed construction chains. Apply aorist scope exclusions to the intensive-causative Lun row; all rows exclude Curadi and use canonical prefixes.
scoring: All rows correct for task success; report per-form accuracy, completed-valid-format accuracy, nasal-spelling sensitivity, refusals and truncations. A contrast set counts as one task.
limitation: A change of scored task unit. This tests consistent selection and application of transformations; it does not establish lower per-form accuracy. Empirical correlation and compute sensitivity must be checked.
sampling: 120 fresh development tasks from 120 distinct families; 360 component forms not previously submitted; no per-item model labels used.
staging: Opus first; submit identical Astra tasks only if useful and within cumulative caps. A negative Opus result is enough to reject a proposed Hard route.
